config/os.go only: getAmazonLinuxVersion now normalises via major(ss[0]) so both '2023 (Amazon Linux)' and a real host's '2023.3.20240219 (Amazon Linux)' map to '2023', keeps YYYY.MM -> '1' (time.Parse "2006.01"), and returns 'unknown' otherwise (base returned '1' for any single-field release, which is the issue's 'fell back to Amazon Linux 1 logic'; it also panicked on an empty release). GetEOL gains 2023/2025/2027/2029. Judgment call: AWS's release-cadence table gives each version an end-of-standard-support (release+2y) and an end-of-maintenance-support (release+5y) date; I put the release+5y retirement date in StandardSupportUntil (2028/2030/2032/2034-03-15) and left ExtendedSupportUntil zero, because Requirements bullet 2 names only StandardSupportUntil, the sibling entries 1/2/2022 already hold full end-of-life dates, and the consumer's warning text ('Purchase extended support if available') would misfire on AL's free maintenance phase. Alternative reading: {Standard: release+2y, Extended: release+5y} - the two differ only for a `now` inside that window. Left scanner/redhatbase.go's AL2023 system-release parsing alone (no bullet names it) since the major() normalisation makes its mangled '2023.x.YYYYMMDD (Amazon' output resolve correctly anyway.
